column1: TC_ID | Title | Preconditions | Steps | Expected Result

WEL-001 | Splash (Arrival) screen displays branding and auto-advances | Fresh app install (onboarding not yet completed) | 1. Launch the app | Splash shows wave logo, "MemoryWave" wordmark, and "Some things are too important to forget." on a dark background with a "TAP ANYWHERE TO BEGIN" pill; after 3 seconds it auto-advances to the Three Truths carousel without any tap

WEL-002 | Tapping the splash advances immediately, before the 3s timer | Fresh app install, splash currently showing | 1. Launch the app 2. Tap anywhere on the splash within 1 second | Screen transitions immediately to the Three Truths carousel (does not wait for the 3s auto-timer)

WEL-003 | Three Truths carousel shows all three cards with correct copy | On the Three Truths screen (post-splash) | 1. View the Three Truths screen | Header "WHAT MEMORYWAVE HOLDS" / "Three things we keep for you."; three cards: "Stories" – "Stories, told in the voices you choose." / "2,400+ audiobooks. Any voice. Any time."; "Voices" (highlighted/accent-filled) – "Voices, preserved before time takes them." / "Record once. Keep forever."; "Presence" – "Presence, kept for whenever you need it." / "The people you love, always within reach."; progress dots show step 1 of 5

WEL-004 | Continue from Three Truths advances to the entry-point question | On the Three Truths screen | 1. Tap "Continue" | Advances to "YOUR ENTRY POINT" / "What brings you to MemoryWave today?" screen; progress dots show step 2 of 5

WEL-005 | Selecting entry-point path 1 (explore audiobooks) is recorded | On the entry-point question screen | 1. Tap "I want to explore audiobooks" card | Card shows a brief pressed/selected animation, then auto-advances to the Privacy page; chosen path is stored as 1 (used later on the auth screen's context line and persisted to prefs key mw_onboarding_path once onboarding finishes)

WEL-006 | Selecting entry-point path 2 (preserve a voice) is recorded | On the entry-point question screen | 1. Tap "I want to preserve someone's voice" card | Advances to Privacy page; chosen path stored as 2 — later the auth screen shows "You're joining to preserve a voice. We'll take good care of it."

WEL-007 | Selecting entry-point path 3 (feel close to someone missed) is recorded | On the entry-point question screen | 1. Tap "I want to feel close to someone I miss" card | Advances to Privacy page; chosen path stored as 3 — later the auth screen shows "You're joining to feel close to someone you miss. We'll take good care of you."

WEL-008 | Entry-point screen does not double-advance on rapid double-tap | On the entry-point question screen | 1. Rapidly tap two different path cards in quick succession | Only the first tap registers (a tap guard ignores further taps while one is already in flight); the app advances once to the Privacy page reflecting only the first-tapped path

WEL-009 | Privacy page shows the three privacy pillars and charter link | On the Privacy page (step 4 of the carousel) | 1. View the Privacy page | Shows "BEFORE WE BEGIN"; body text "Every voice you bring here belongs to you. We hold it with the care it deserves."; three pillars: "Always encrypted" / "Protected at rest and in transit", "Never shared" / "We will never sell or share your voices", "Yours to keep or delete" / "Remove any voice, completely, at any time"; button "I understand — let's begin"; link text "Our complete Voice Privacy Charter →"; progress dots show step 4 of 5

WEL-010 | Completing onboarding lands on the auth (sign-up/sign-in) screen | On the Privacy page | 1. Tap "I understand — let's begin" | Onboarding completion is persisted (prefs mw_onboarding_done=true, mw_onboarding_path=<chosen path>); app navigates to the auth screen ("Create your MemoryWave")

WEL-011 | Onboarding is not shown again on a subsequent app launch | Onboarding already completed once on this device (mw_onboarding_done=true), user not logged in | 1. Force-close the app 2. Relaunch it | App skips the entire Welcome flow (splash/carousel/privacy) and opens directly to the auth screen

WEL-012 | "Voice Privacy Charter" link is present but not verified to navigate anywhere in this codebase pass | On the Privacy page | 1. Tap "Our complete Voice Privacy Charter →" | Record actual behavior — this text render as a plain Text widget with no onTap handler visible in welcome_screen.dart at the time of this review; confirm whether it is inert (no-op) or wired elsewhere

LGN-001 | Auth screen shows correct context line for chosen path 1 | Onboarding completed with path 1 (explore audiobooks) selected | 1. Reach the auth screen | Text reads "You're joining to explore audiobooks. 2,400+ titles are waiting." with "explore audiobooks." in accent color

LGN-002 | "I already have an account" reveals the inline sign-in form | On the auth screen, sign-in form collapsed | 1. Tap "I already have an account" | Button label toggles to "Hide sign-in"; an inline card appears below with "WELCOME BACK", Email field, Password field, "Sign in" button, and the note "First sign-in includes a short face & voice verification."
LGN-003 | "Hide sign-in" collapses the inline sign-in form | Sign-in form currently expanded | 1. Tap "Hide sign-in" | Form collapses (animated), button label reverts to "I already have an account"

LGN-004 | Email is required | Sign-in form expanded | 1. Leave Email blank 2. Enter any password 3. Tap "Sign in" | Inline validation under the Email field reads "Email is required"; no network call is made

LGN-005 | Email must contain "@" (client-side check is presence-of-@ only, not a full email regex) | Sign-in form expanded | 1. Enter an email with no "@" character (e.g. "not-an-email") 2. Enter any password 3. Tap "Sign in" | Inline validation reads "Enter a valid email"; no network call is made. Note: any string containing "@" (e.g. "a@b") passes this client check regardless of overall validity — worth a follow-up case

LGN-005b | A minimally-"valid" string containing only "@" passes client-side email validation | Sign-in form expanded | 1. Enter "a@b" as the email 2. Enter any password 3. Tap "Sign in" | No client-side "Enter a valid email" error is shown (the check is only `.contains('@')`); the request proceeds to the backend, which will independently reject it — confirm actual backend response text

LGN-006 | Password is required | Sign-in form expanded | 1. Enter a valid-looking email 2. Leave Password blank 3. Tap "Sign in" | Inline validation under the Password field reads "Password is required"; no network call is made

LGN-007 | Invalid credentials show the correct backend-derived error | Sign-in form expanded; credentials that do not match any account | 1. Enter a non-existent (or wrong-password) email/password pair 2. Tap "Sign in" | Snackbar reads "Invalid email or password." (mapped from HTTP 401); user remains on the auth screen, not logged in

LGN-008 | Disabled account shows the correct error | Sign-in form expanded; an account known to be disabled server-side (HTTP 403) | 1. Enter that account's credentials 2. Tap "Sign in" | Snackbar reads "This account is disabled."

LGN-009 | Network failure during login shows a generic connectivity error | Sign-in form expanded; device offline or backend unreachable | 1. Enter any credentials 2. Tap "Sign in" | Snackbar reads "Could not reach the server. Check your connection."

LGN-010 | Successful login with an already-verified account goes straight to Home (no re-verification) | Sign-in form expanded; account previously completed First-Login Verification on this exact device (local isVerified flag set for that user id) | 1. Enter that account's correct credentials 2. Tap "Sign in" | Snackbar reads "Login successful."; app navigates directly to the Home shell (skips Verification screen), since isVerified is tracked locally per user id and was already set

LGN-011 | Successful login with a never-verified account routes to Verification | Sign-in form expanded; account has correct credentials but has never completed verification on this device (or app data was cleared since) | 1. Enter correct credentials 2. Tap "Sign in" | Snackbar reads "Login successful."; app navigates to the First-Login Verification screen

LGN-012 | "Sign in" button shows a loading state and disables other controls while submitting | Sign-in form expanded, valid credentials entered | 1. Tap "Sign in" and immediately observe the button and the "Begin with Email" / toggle buttons | "Sign in" button shows its loading indicator; "Begin with Email" and the show/hide sign-in toggle become disabled (onPressed: null) until the request completes

LGN-013 | Apple sign-in is a stub, not implemented | On the auth screen | 1. Tap "Apple" | Snackbar reads "Apple sign-in arrives with the real backend."; no navigation occurs, no account is created or logged in

LGN-014 | Google sign-in is a stub, not implemented | On the auth screen | 1. Tap "Google" | Snackbar reads "Google sign-in arrives with the real backend."; no navigation occurs, no account is created or logged in

LGN-015 | "Begin with Email" opens the Registration screen | On the auth screen | 1. Tap "Begin with Email" | Navigates to the Registration screen ("Begin with Email" / "A few details, and your MemoryWave is yours.")

LGN-016 | Logging out and back in with the same account skips verification again | User is logged in, verified, and on Home | 1. Log out 2. On the auth screen, sign in again with the same account's credentials | Snackbar "Login successful."; app goes straight to Home again — logout only clears the session token, it does not clear the locally-stored isVerified flag for that user id

VER-001 | First-Login Verification screen shows correct step-by-step instructions and initial state | User just logged in or registered with an unverified account, camera permission not yet decided | 1. Reach the Verification screen | Title "First-Login Verification"; instructions "Press Start, keep speaking continuously, and follow the head-turn prompts. Detection is automatic."; status row shows "Face marker OFF" and "Pose not locked"; a "Start Verification" button is present

VER-002 | Camera permission prompt appears and camera initializes when granted | Verification screen just opened, camera permission not yet granted, first attempt to use the camera this install | 1. Reach the Verification screen 2. Respond "While using the app" (or "Allow") to the camera permission prompt | Camera preview begins rendering the live front-camera feed inside the preview box; "Start Verification" button becomes enabled

VER-003 | Denying camera permission shows the correct error and disables verification | Verification screen open, camera permission prompt showing | 1. Deny camera permission ("Don't allow") | Preview area shows an error: "Camera could not be initialized: CameraException(CameraAccessDenied, Camera access permission was denied.)"; "Start Verification" button is disabled (camera not ready)

VER-004 | No camera available on the device is handled with a specific message | Device/emulator reports zero available cameras | 1. Reach the Verification screen | Error text reads "No camera found on this device." |

VER-005 | Starting verification without microphone permission fails with a specific message | Camera ready; microphone permission not granted | 1. Tap "Start Verification" without microphone permission | Verification start fails with "Failed to start verification: Exception: Microphone permission is required."; recording does not start

VER-006 | Step 1 of 3: "Look FORWARD" must be held steady before advancing | Verification started (recording in progress), on step 1 of 3 | 1. Face the camera straight on and hold | "Face marker" turns to a positive/green state once a valid face is detected; once yaw is within ±10° of forward for ~3 consecutive stable frames, a hold countdown begins (default 2s per code, though the on-screen "3 dots" progress and step counter reflect 3 total steps: Look FORWARD, Turn LEFT, Turn RIGHT — note the order differs from the standalone voice-recording liveness widget, which uses forward/right/left); holding for the full countdown advances to step 2

VER-007 | Losing the pose mid-countdown cancels the hold and requires re-matching | Verification in progress, hold countdown active for the current step | 1. Turn away from the target pose before the countdown reaches 0 | Countdown cancels (pose match reset to false); the step's target instruction remains active and the user must re-achieve and re-hold the pose to progress

VER-008 | Switching to a different face mid-check resets pose-hold progress | Verification in progress, one face already being tracked | 1. Have a second/different face enter frame such that ML Kit assigns a new tracking id | Pose-hold progress resets to 0 for the new tracking id rather than crediting an in-progress hold to the new face

VER-009 | A face too small or too near the frame edge is not counted as a valid face | Verification in progress | 1. Move the face far from the camera (small in frame) or to the extreme edge of frame | "Face marker" stays off / pose is not evaluated as matched — face is rejected by the area-ratio (≥4% of frame) and center-position bounds checks even though ML Kit technically detected something

VER-010 | All three poses held in order completes verification and saves local audio/video | All three head-pose steps (Look FORWARD, Turn LEFT, Turn RIGHT) held successfully in sequence | 1. Complete step 1 (Look FORWARD) 2. Complete step 2 3. Complete step 3 | Recording stops; success message "Verification successful. Audio and video recorded locally." is shown; app then calls the completion callback, which sets the account's isVerified flag locally and shows a second snackbar "Verification complete."; app navigates to Home

VER-011 | Verification completion sets a per-account local flag, not a server-side one | Verification just completed successfully | 1. Complete verification 2. (Separately, out of scope for UI testing) inspect that no verification-status API call was made | isVerified is stored only in local SharedPreferences keyed by the user's id (verified_v1_<id>) — there is no backend endpoint for this per the code's own comment; reinstalling the app or clearing app data will require verification again for the same account

VER-012 | Recorded audio missing/empty produces a specific failure message | Verification flow reaches the finish step but the audio file is missing or 0 bytes (e.g. recorder failure) | 1. Complete the pose sequence in a state where audio recording failed | Failure handled via "Verification failed: Exception: Audio was not recorded." (or "...Audio file was not saved." / "...Audio file is empty." depending on which check trips); recording/camera state is cleanly reset, error shown, "Start Verification" re-enabled

VER-013 | Recorded video missing/empty produces a specific failure message | Verification flow reaches the finish step but the video file is missing or 0 bytes | 1. Complete the pose sequence in a state where video recording failed | Failure handled via "Verification failed: Exception: Video was not recorded." (or "...Video file was not saved." / "...Video file is empty."); state resets, error shown, retry possible

VER-014 | "Restart Verification" is available after a failure and resets the flow | Verification screen showing an error state (e.g. after a failure or camera error) | 1. Tap "Restart Verification" | All in-progress state clears (step resets to 0, face/pose flags reset, error/success messages cleared); user can attempt "Start Verification" again from the beginning

VER-015 | Backing out of the app mid-verification does not crash and releases the camera | Verification in progress (recording active) | 1. Background the app or navigate away mid-recording (e.g. Home button) | Camera controller, audio recorder, and face detector are disposed cleanly (dispose() stops the image stream, disposes the camera controller, audio recorder, and face detector); no crash on return

VER-016 | Yaw sign convention: turning head LEFT vs RIGHT maps to the correct on-screen instruction | Verification in progress, on the "Turn LEFT" or "Turn RIGHT" step | 1. On "Turn LEFT", turn head to the user's actual left 2. On "Turn RIGHT", turn to the user's actual right | Each turn is matched to its corresponding step per the code's yaw-sign convention (documented in code as: on the unmirrored front camera buffer, turning left gives positive yaw, right gives negative — flag as a device-dependent risk if a given device/mirroring setup reports inverted signs, since the code comments explicitly note this may need flipping per device)

REG-001 | Registration form required-field validation (empty submit) | On the Registration screen, all fields blank | 1. Tap "Create my MemoryWave" with all fields empty | "Name is required" under Full name; "Email is required" under Email; "Password must be at least 8 characters" under Password (0 < 8 chars counts as too short — there is no separate empty-password message on this screen, unlike Login); Confirm password has no independent empty check beyond the mismatch rule

REG-002 | Email must contain "@" on the Registration form too | Name and passwords valid | 1. Enter an email with no "@" 2. Fill other fields validly 3. Submit | "Enter a valid email" shown under Email; same relaxed check as Login (`.contains('@')` only)

REG-003 | Password must be at least 8 characters | Name/email valid, password under 8 characters (e.g. "short") | 1. Enter a 5-character password 2. Match it in Confirm password 3. Submit | "Password must be at least 8 characters" shown under Password

REG-004 | Password exactly 8 characters is accepted by client-side validation | Name/email valid | 1. Enter an 8-character password 2. Match it in Confirm password 3. Submit | No password-length validation error (the check is strictly `< 8`, so 8 passes); request proceeds to the backend

REG-005 | Confirm password must exactly match Password | Name/email valid, password ≥ 8 chars | 1. Enter a password 2. Enter a different string in Confirm password 3. Submit | "Passwords do not match" shown under Confirm password; no network call made

REG-006 | Registering with an email that already exists shows the correct backend-derived error | Name/password fields valid; email belongs to an existing account | 1. Enter an already-registered email 2. Fill remaining fields validly 3. Submit | Snackbar reads "An account with this email already exists." (mapped from HTTP 409); user remains on the Registration screen

REG-007 | Network failure during registration shows a generic connectivity error | Form valid; device offline or backend unreachable | 1. Submit a valid new registration while offline | Snackbar reads "Could not reach the server. Check your connection."

REG-008 | Successful registration logs the user in immediately and proceeds to Verification, despite the success message implying a separate login step | Form filled with a genuinely new, unused email and valid matching passwords ≥8 chars | 1. Submit the form | Snackbar reads "Registration successful. Please log in." — BUT the register API response already returns auth tokens, which the app stores and treats as an active session immediately (see auth_service.dart _completeAuth); the very next screen is First-Login Verification, not the Login screen. This is a real copy/behavior mismatch worth flagging to the team, not a test artifact

REG-009 | "Create my MemoryWave" shows a loading state while submitting | Form valid | 1. Submit 2. Immediately observe the submit button | Button shows its loading indicator until the request completes

REG-010 | "I already have an account" link returns to the Login screen without submitting | On the Registration screen, form partially or fully filled | 1. Tap "I already have an account" | Navigates back to the Login/auth screen; no registration request is sent; any entered data is discarded (fields are on a screen that gets disposed)

REG-011 | Full name field only checks for non-empty after trimming (no character/format restriction observed) | On the Registration screen | 1. Enter a name consisting only of leading/trailing spaces 2. Fill other fields validly 3. Submit | "Name is required" is shown, since the validator trims before checking emptiness; a name of only whitespace is rejected. A name with digits/symbols, however, passes client-side validation with no format restriction — confirm whether the backend enforces anything stricter
